The Historical Agricultural Forecast Database (HAFD) records what was
forecast, when it was issued, and the later actual used for comparison.
`read_agau_forecast_history()` normalises its CSV or workbook schema while
retaining source identity and a SHA-256 hash for the exact bytes read.

The two files used below are small package-owned synthetic fixtures. They
exercise the CSV and workbook fingerprints without redistributing an official
database or asserting that the example values are current.

## Read CSV and workbook inputs

Start with an explicit local path for a deterministic, offline workflow. A
temporary cache keeps any parser metadata out of the home directory.

```{r setup}
library(readagau)

fixture_root <- system.file("fixtures", package = "readagau")
csv_file <- file.path(fixture_root, "workbooks", "historical-forecast.csv")
xlsx_file <- file.path(fixture_root, "workbooks", "historical-forecast.xlsx")
stopifnot(file.exists(csv_file), file.exists(xlsx_file))

hafd_cache <- tempfile("readagau-hafd-")
dir.create(hafd_cache)

hafd_csv <- read_agau_forecast_history(csv_file, cache_dir = hafd_cache)
hafd_xlsx <- read_agau_forecast_history(xlsx_file, cache_dir = hafd_cache)
```

Both paths produce an `agau_forecast_history` tibble. The parser chooses the
single workbook sheet with the required field fingerprint; it does not guess
from a sheet position. CSV and workbook inputs share the same semantic
columns, while their `sha256` values correctly differ because the source bytes
are different.

```{r hafd-preview}
hafd_csv[
  , c(
    "commodity", "estimate_type", "unit", "region", "year_issued",
    "month_issued", "year_issued_fy", "forecast_year_fy",
    "original_forecast", "latest_actual"
  )
]
```

## Output contract and missing values

The result has 15 columns: commodity and estimate descriptors; issue year and
month; issue and forecast financial years; numeric `original_forecast` and
`latest_actual`; and `release_id`, `source_url`, `retrieved_at`, and `sha256`.
Year fields are integer where they represent a year, forecasts are doubles,
and published missing markers such as `..` become `NA` rather than zero.

```{r hafd-provenance}
hafd_csv[
  , c("release_id", "source_url", "retrieved_at", "sha256")
]
```

The local example uses `release_id = "historical-forecast-local"` and has no
official URL. When a release is discovered from a landing page, the returned
`release_id`, `source_url`, retrieval time, and content hash identify the
asset that was actually parsed.

## Discovery and cache replay

The package can discover the HAFD workbook from its landing page when
`path = NULL`. To keep this vignette offline, the option below points to the
small packaged landing-page fixture; its relative workbook link resolves to
the packaged synthetic workbook. The same reader call and cache machinery are
used for an official landing page, but an official call requires network
access and should be made only when the source is available and its terms have
been checked.

```{r local-discovery}
landing_fixture <- file.path(fixture_root, "html", "historical-forecasts.html")
withr::local_options(list(readagau.hafd_landing_url = landing_fixture))

discovered <- read_agau_forecast_history(
  path = NULL,
  cache_dir = hafd_cache
)
discovered[
  , c("release_id", "source_url", "original_forecast", "sha256")
]
```

With `refresh = FALSE`, an existing valid cached asset is replayed without
re-fetching the landing page or downloading the workbook. Use `refresh = TRUE`
only when an intentional source refresh is required; retain the resulting
hash and release metadata with downstream outputs.

## Typed schema failures

Malformed numeric fields are rejected with a typed `agau_schema_error`. This
example writes a one-off malformed copy below `tempdir()` solely to show the
failure contract; it does not alter the packaged fixture.

```{r typed-failure}
malformed <- utils::read.csv(
  csv_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
malformed$original_forecast <- "not a published missing marker"
malformed_file <- tempfile("readagau-hafd-malformed-", fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(malformed, malformed_file, row.names = FALSE)

failure <- tryCatch(
  read_agau_forecast_history(malformed_file, cache_dir = hafd_cache),
  agau_schema_error = function(e) e
)
stopifnot(inherits(failure, "agau_schema_error"))
failure
```

Downstream code should branch on the `agau_schema_error` or
`agau_asset_missing_error` class and preserve the diagnostic fields, rather
than treating a malformed source as an empty forecast history.

## Optional live discovery

The live path is deliberately guarded so that normal vignette and CRAN builds
remain deterministic and network-free. Set `READAGAU_RUN_LIVE=true` in an
interactive session only after confirming network access and the publisher's
current attribution and redistribution terms. Use a managed cache and record
the returned `sha256` when using live data.

```{r live-hafd, eval=TRUE}
if (interactive() && identical(Sys.getenv("READAGAU_RUN_LIVE"), "true")) {
  live_hafd <- read_agau_forecast_history(
    path = NULL,
    refresh = TRUE,
    cache_dir = hafd_cache
  )
  utils::head(live_hafd)
}
```

For reproducible package examples, tests, and analyses, use an explicit local
asset such as the packaged CSV or workbook and keep its hash with the output.
